reviews.reason: Eating already handles intake, but no implemented capability prepares food for later consumption. A minimal feasible preparation is crushing safe roots using an acquired stone and bark work surface. It requires no assumed fire, equipment or new food stock. Preparation preserves nutrition rather than creating additional nutrition or detoxification.
reviews.experienceReview: Crushing alone does not earn wellbeing, and there is no established physical reason for a nutrition bonus. Actual eating can provide bounded enjoyment of a substantial safe meal, including repeated enjoyment. Bind one canonical food-enjoyment rule to meal-experience, shared with raw and preserved food rather than a preparation-specific alias: participant is the actual eater; require at least 8 nutrition actually accepted within the existing 10-round meal window, nonspoiled nontoxic food, and a positive appetite at intake. Award 0.4 transient pleasure, source cap 0.8, duration 4 rounds, refresh rather than stack, cooldown 10 rounds per eater across all food forms. Emit at most once for the same intake window; no reward for discarded overflow or processing. This finite meal does not establish a maintained satisfaction source. A separately performed qualifying experiment may use the existing information-confirmed rule through probe, never an automatic reward for completing preparation.
reviews.visualReview: Show the real stone, bark surface and reserved roots at the work location, followed by a visibly crushed food stack only after completion. Display remaining work, paid energy, original ingredients, nutrition, spoilage and the absence of cooking or preservation. Replay paid crushing steps and completion/cancellation using the declared process events; no meal, warmth or wellbeing animation occurs merely on registration or learning.
reviews.specification: Implement root-preparation-v1. Public schema: {operation:'prepare', inputStackId, quantity, stoneId, barkId, processId?}; use shared actor/item/object/process references, world coordinates, mass units and simulation rounds. Require living actor, individual mastery, positive integral quantity, owned unspoiled meadow roots, an actual owned stone unit and bark unit, and placement on accessible, unoccupied ground within 0.65 interaction distance. Stone and bark are reusable implements, unavailable for simultaneous conflicting operations; acquire them separately. No fire or water is required. Record input identities, quantity, accumulated spoilage, composition, harvest history, tool references, owner, location, remaining work and paid energy. Perform two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round, including setup and crushing. Reserve roots in uniquely owned process escrow; continue their actual decay. Each paid round reduces remaining work exactly once. Pause on movement out of reach or insufficient energy. Completion atomically converts escrow into crushed-root food owned by the actor; conserve edible mass, 14 nutrition per input root, zero initial toxicity, and original provenance. No washing, sterilization or extended shelf life is implied; crushed food decays at 1.25 times its corresponding unprocessed rate and never resets accumulated spoilage. Existing eat must accept this composition and apply normal satiety, toxicity and spoilage rules, without direct healing. Cancellation, including death, releases the actual unfinished crushed/raw mixture at the process location with its current composition and decay; spent effort is not refunded, and escrow is neither duplicated nor deleted. Tools remain actual world items. The work patch is a non-solid radius-0.3 ground footprint, cannot overlap incompatible occupied work surfaces, and creates no room, shade or collision barrier. Declare food-preparation-started and food-preparation-completed; bind paid updates and cancellation to process-progress, process-completed and process-stopped. Dependencies are item reservation, composite edible state, existing decay/eat and shared geometry; implement these in this handoff. Migrate existing stacks unchanged; add processing history only to transformed portions. Keep implementation, individual study and actual execution separate.

reviews.reason: No existing function slows spoilage. A small air-drying tray for crushed safe roots is a feasible precursor that requires actual materials and suitable weather. Its effectiveness must depend on measured moisture and exposure, not a preservation label. The two carried roots remain ordinary roots until processing actually occurs.
reviews.experienceReview: A completed tray or drying label is not itself pleasure or sustained satisfaction. The measurable benefit is slower subsequent decay while the food remains sufficiently dry. Actual consumption may receive the same canonical meal-experience food-enjoyment rule specified for preparation: actual eater, at least 8 accepted nutrition in a 10-round window, safe nonspoiled intake and positive appetite; 0.4 pleasure, cap 0.8, duration 4, refresh only, 10-round shared food cooldown and one grant per intake window. It is not an additional preserved-food reward. No maintained satisfaction is inferred from unattended storage. A real comparison establishing previously unconfirmed spoilage behavior can qualify through probe and the existing information-confirmed source, subject to that source's novelty, cap and cooldown rules.
reviews.visualReview: Render the acquired stones and bark as a small ground tray with only the food actually loaded. Show paid setup/crushing progress, moisture, drying or rain-paused status, accumulated spoilage and current decay multiplier. Bind shrinking food mass and rewetting to food-drying-progress and food-rewetted; completion changes appearance only when the moisture threshold is reached. Replay water transfers and actual material placement, and clearly distinguish predicted drying work from completed preserved food.
reviews.specification: Implement root-air-drying-v1. Public schema: {operation:'build'|'load'|'unload'|'dismantle', processId?, trayId?, inputStackId?, quantity?, stoneIds?, barkId?, x?, y?}. Use the same shared reference, coordinate, mass and process contracts as root preparation. Independently implement drying; record reuse of its crushing, food-provenance and escrow code as code reuse, not functional equivalence or personal mastery. Build requires two actual stone units and one bark unit, accessible ground and a living trained actor. Reserve these materials; two active rounds at 1 energy each assemble a non-solid radius-0.4 tray, capacity two root units, with 0.65 interaction reach. Validate shared placement against obstacles and incompatible work footprints. Materials remain conserved components and cannot simultaneously serve another process. Loading requires owned unspoiled meadow roots; crush on the tray using a support stone for two active rounds per root at 1 energy per round. Record all original food composition, harvest and decay history. Root wet mass starts from its actual resource composition: water 50%, other mass 50%; nutrition remains 14 per original root, toxicity zero. After loading, drying is passive, with explicit remaining water-removal work. At each dt=1, when uncovered, not raining and temperature is between 10 and 40 C, remove at most 0.005 mass units of water per root and never below a water fraction of 0.12; transfer removed water to the environmental water ledger. At other temperatures pause drying. Rain adds actual environmental water at up to 0.01 mass per root per round, bounded by the original 50% water fraction. Resolve temperature, rain, cover and exposure from shared weather and geometry, not applicant labels; add a conservative explicit weather-state field if necessary rather than assume favorable conditions. Before dry completion, use crushed-food decay at 1.25 times baseline; at water fraction <=0.12 use 0.35 times baseline while actually dry. Rewetting above 0.12 immediately removes that benefit. Never reset accumulated spoilage, reverse spoiled food, remove toxins or increase nutrients. Completion emits a dried composite food stack retained in the tray; unload transfers that actual stack to inventory. Away from the tray, continue tracking moisture, rain exposure, decay and provenance; no automatic waterproof container. Existing eat consumes its real composition. Owner, component identities, escrow, work progress, moisture, environmental transfers and decay persist. Pause active work on lost reach or energy. Any multi-round actor operation cancels on death, leaving uniquely owned materials and the actual partly processed food at the tray; passive exposure remains physical state, not a dead actor's continuing action. Manual cancellation follows the same rule, without refunds or duplication. Dismantling takes one round and 1 energy, returns actual components at their current condition and deposits any food unchanged. Declare drying-tray-built, food-drying-progress, food-drying-completed and food-rewetted, plus process-progress/process-completed/process-stopped for active work. Dependencies include shared weather/geometry, food water-mass accounting, decay, eat and process ownership; implement within this handoff. Existing foods retain their original decay history; migrate root water composition without changing mass or nutrition. No stock, tray or mastery is supplied by development.
